subject: ArrTags task 15.2 - Thread the bounded log subject through the identity-bearing and fallback sites (ADR-026 clause 3)

findings.description: The reader-threw metadata-read-failure path is a distinct subject substitution that the new tests never exercise. The only MetadataReadFailed theory drives the failed-read result path (FakeMetadataReader.Result = ArrMetadataReadResult.Failure(...)); no test configures a reader that throws, so the catch-block subject at MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:159 is unverified. The worker report and the v1.2 changelog claim both provider-error paths are covered by MetadataReadFailureSubjectIsTheFileNameOnlyAtEveryVerbosity, which overstates what the suite establishes: a regression that changes only the catch-path subject (for example back to the raw item id, or a path-bearing variant) passes the whole suite.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogRedactionTests.cs:952-984 (DriveMetadataReadFailureAsync sets Result = Failure; never a throwing reader or throwing Handler)
src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:154-168 (reader-threw catch subject) versus :171-187 (failed-read result subject) are two separate LogSubject.Create call sites
docs/implementation/15.2/worker-report.json acceptance_criteria[1] names both paths as verified by the theory; docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md:57-59 repeats the two-path claim

Independent probe: changed only the catch-path subject (MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:159) to LogSubject.Create(identity.JellyfinItemId) (item-id only, no file name); rebuilt (0 warnings / 0 errors) and LogRedactionTests still passed 125/125 (0 failed). Source restored from a byte-identical backup and verified via sha256sum -c: OK
findings.recommended_action: Add one case (or theory) that drives the reader-threw catch path with a FakeMetadataReader.Handler that throws, with a path-bearing and a pathless identity, and assert the same file-name-only / item-id-fallback subjects; or narrow the worker report and changelog claims to the failed-read path that is actually covered.

findings.description: The LibraryWorkWorker retry-scheduled subject substitution is not exercised. DriveQueueAsync uses RecordingWorkItemProcessor, which always returns a non-retryable Completed result, so LogRetryScheduled is never reached. The worker report and changelog cite LogProcessed and LogRetryScheduled together as covered by WorkWorkerSubjectIsTheItemIdAtEveryVerbosity, but only LogProcessed is on the exercised path.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Updates/LibraryWorkWorker.cs:255-269 (LogRetryScheduled subject) is a separate call site from :233-247 (LogProcessed)
docs/implementation/15.2/worker-report.json acceptance_criteria[4] evidence names LogProcessed/LogRetryScheduled; docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md:70-72 names both records

Independent probe: set the retry subject (LibraryWorkWorker.cs:262) to LogSubject.Create(System.Guid.Empty); rebuilt (0 warnings / 0 errors) and LogRedactionTests still passed 125/125 (0 failed). Source restored byte-identically (sha256sum -c: OK)
findings.recommended_action: Add a queue case whose processor returns a retryable result for one attempt so LogRetryScheduled is emitted, and assert the item-id subject on the WorkItemRetryScheduled record; or drop LogRetryScheduled from the coverage claim.

findings.description: The fallback (identity present but no usable primary path) branch is site-tested at the mixed discard site and at the metadata-read-failure site only. The identity-bearing artwork and Radarr/Sonarr reader fallbacks are not driven without a path; they rely on the shared helper's unit tests (LogSubjectTests, task 15.1) plus one representative site-level fallback test. Residual risk is low because those sites pass `identity.MediaLocation?.PrimaryPath` into the same helper and the null-path behavior is thoroughly unit-tested.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogRedactionTests.cs:1130-1149 (SentinelIdentity always has primaryPath) and :1180-1205 (SentinelEpisodeIdentity always has primaryPath); DriveMatchingAsync/DriveSonarrMatchingAsync/DriveArtworkAsync never construct a pathless identity
findings.recommended_action: No action required for 15.2; recorded for traceability. If a future task wants per-site fallback proof, add pathless-identity variants of the artwork and reader theories.

findings.description: Of the 60 new theory cases, roughly half run at verbosity levels where the line is gated off and assert only that the record count is 0 (the sentinel scan over an empty record list is vacuous). This is honest and sufficient - count 0 is itself the gating assertion and no output can leak - but the phrase 'at every verbosity level' in the test remarks/worker report should not be read as a subject assertion at every level; the subject is asserted at the enabled levels (30 cases).
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogRedactionTests.cs:200-417 (early `if (expected == 0) return;` on all ten new theories; AssertNoSentinel is called but iterates no records at gated levels)
findings.recommended_action: No action required; the pattern is accurate as written.

findings.description: The 15.2 change is reported against the default suite only (1577/63/1640). The canonical release matrix in docs/release/build-and-release.md still records the 1.1.0.0 counts (1513/44/1557 host-guarded, 1575/20/1595 forced-native). This is not a 15.2 test-quality gap: the new tests are not host-gated or native-gated, and the worker's known_limitations state the current-state surfaces are updated by task 15.4. Host-guarded and forced-native were not rerun for this audit.
evidence: docs/implementation/15.2/worker-report.json known_limitations[2] (15.4 owns the canonical documentation reconciliation)
findings.recommended_action: No action for 15.2; task 15.4 / the release task must refresh the matrix once Phase 15 closes.

substitutes_checked: ArrTagsLog<T> + LogVerbosityGate are the real production log facade/gate; only the host ILogger is captured (CapturingLoggerProvider/CapturingLogger<T>), so gating behavior is real and observed.

MetadataReconciliationProcessor, ArtworkGenerationCoordinator, RadarrMetadataReader, SonarrMetadataReader, LibraryWorkWorker, and ArrTagsLifecycleService are real production classes; the subject under test is built inside them, not in a double.
FakeMetadataReader / FakeRadarrReadClient / FakeSonarrReadClient / FakeReadClientFactory substitute only the external Arr HTTP-provider boundary.
ReconciliationLibraryResolver, ReconciliationTestMovie, FakeMediaLibraryEnumerator substitute the Jellyfin library boundary; MediaIdentityFactory and MediaIdentity are production.
PipelineArtworkHost and FingerprintingRenderer substitute only the host image read/write boundary; ArtworkPublisher/state stores are production.

RecordingWorkItemProcessor, RecordingWorkHintSink, NoOpLifecycleCoordinator, and FakeLibraryEventSource are queue/lifecycle boundary doubles; the worker and lifecycle service that build the subject are production.
TestTimeProvider isolates LogThrottle from wall-clock time.
skips_checked: The 10 new theories carry no skip guard (no [Fact(Skip)], no environment gate); the focused run reported 0 skipped.
The full default run reported 63 skipped, identical to the post-15.1 baseline, so 0 new skips (matches the worker claim).

The 63 skips are the environment/host-gated facts documented at docs/release/build-and-release.md:79-85 (19 pinned-host + 43 ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT-native + 1 ARRTAGS_NONCANONICAL_GOLDENS); none of the ADR-026 subject behavior depends on them.
determinism_checked: New tests use static verbosity data, InvariantCulture and StringComparison.Ordinal; no clock, culture, machine-name, or network input affects any assertion.
Each test constructs its own CapturingLoggerProvider and a unique temp state root (Path.GetTempPath() + Guid), so there is no shared mutable state or order dependence.
LogThrottle uses TestTimeProvider with a fixed epoch; no wall-clock dependence in the new theories.
The pre-existing webhook wait uses a bounded polling loop (WaitForRecordAsync) but is not on any new 15.2 theory path.
Repeated focused runs (before and after restore) both reported 125/125, and the full default run matched the worker count exactly.
summary: The task-15.2 tests are genuinely meaningful on the paths they exercise: they drive the real production coordinator/processor/readers/worker/lifecycle classes with doubles only at external boundaries, assert the positive exact subject substring ('item example.mkv' / 'item s02e05.mkv') plus the absence of '/' and of the replaced item id (so a full-path regression fails, not just a missing-name check), and reproduce the reported counts exactly (focused 125/125; default 1577 passed / 63 skipped / 1640 total; +60 / 0 new skips). No tautologies or wrong-reason passes were found. Two concrete coverage gaps remain. First (MEDIUM), the reader-threw metadata-read-failure path is a separate subject call site that no test drives, yet the worker report and changelog claim both provider-error paths are verified; an independent probe reverting only that catch-path subject to the item-id-only form was not caught (125/125 still passed). Second (LOW), LibraryWorkWorker.LogRetryScheduled is named as covered but the retry branch is never reached, and a probe corrupting its subject was likewise not caught. Both probed files were restored byte-identically (sha256 verified) and the tree is unchanged. The remaining observations (unexercised site-level fallback for artwork/readers, gated-off cases asserting only record count 0, and the still-stale 1.1.0.0 release matrix owned by task 15.4) are informational. Because no BLOCKER or HIGH finding is open, the status is PASS_WITH_FINDINGS.
